babs.5: Bodily contact with a menstruating woman
babs.6: The menstruating woman leaving the fast
babs.7: The menstruating woman performs all the rites except circling the House
babs.10: May a woman pray in a garment in which she menstruated?
babs.11: Perfume for the woman when bathing after menstruation
babs.12: A woman rubbing herself when purifying from menstruation
babs.14: A woman combing her hair when bathing after menstruation
babs.15: A woman undoing her hair for the bath after menstruation
babs.17: How the menstruating woman enters iḥrām for ḥajj and ʿumra
babs.18: The onset and end of menstruation
babs.19: The menstruating woman does not make up the prayer
babs.20: Sleeping with a menstruating woman while she is in her clothes
babs.21: Menstruating women attend the two ʿĪds and the Muslims' supplication and keep away from the prayer place
babs.22: If she menstruates three times in a month, and what women are believed in regarding menstruation
babs.23: Yellowish and turbid discharge outside the days of menstruation

babs.27: The funeral prayer for a woman in childbed and its sunna

294.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim say: I heard al-Qāsim say: I heard ʿĀʾisha say: “We set out intending nothing but Ḥajj. When we were at Sarif, I menstruated. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to me while I was weeping. He said: What is the matter with you, have you menstruated? I said: Yes. He said: This is a matter that Allah has decreed for the daughters of Ādam. So do what the pilgrim does, except do not circumambulate the House. She said: And the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed cows on behalf of his wives.”
294.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “How menstruation began.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she began to menstruate at Sarif on the pilgrimage and wept. The Prophet tells her this is something Allah decreed for the daughters of Ādam, and instructs her to do everything the pilgrim does except circumambulate the House. At the end it is mentioned that the Prophet sacrificed cows on behalf of his wives.

295.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “I used to comb the head of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while I was menstruating.”
295.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The menstruating woman washing and combing her husband’s head.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she combed the Prophet’s head while she was menstruating.

296.matn: Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā narrated to us, he said: Hishām ibn Yūsuf narrated to us that Ibn Jurayj told them, he said: Hishām told me, from ʿUrwa, that he was asked: “May a menstruating woman serve me, or may a woman come near me while she is junub? ʿUrwa said: All of that is easy for me, and each of those serves me, and there is no harm in any of it for anyone. ʿĀʾisha told me that she used to comb – meaning the head of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace – while she was menstruating, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was then secluded in the mosque, bringing his head close to her while she was in her room, and she would comb it while she was menstruating.”
296.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “The menstruating woman washing and combing her husband’s head.” It is a statement of ʿUrwa, who, when asked, declares service by a menstruating woman unobjectionable and relies on ʿĀʾisha’s report. He then reports that the Prophet was secluded in the mosque, inclined his head toward her, and she combed it in her room.

297.matn: Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, he heard Zuhayr, from Manṣūr ibn Ṣafiyya: His mother told him: ʿĀʾisha told her that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “used to lean in my lap while I was menstruating, and then recite the Qur’an.”
297.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A man reciting in his wife’s lap while she is menstruating.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet leaned in her lap while she was menstruating and then recited the Qur’an.

298.matn: al-Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Salama: Zaynab, the daughter of Umm Salama, told him: Umm Salama told her, she said: “While I was lying with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in a cloak (khamīṣa), I menstruated. So I slipped away and took my menstruation clothes. He said: Have you menstruated? I said: Yes. Then he called me, and I lay down with him in the soft blanket (khamīla).”
298.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “A man reciting in his wife’s lap while she is menstruating.” Umm Salama reports that she was lying with the Prophet, began to menstruate, withdrew and took her menstruation clothes, and that he then called her, so she lay down with him again.

299.matn: Qabīṣa narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “I used to wash together with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from a single vessel, both of us being junub,
299.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bodily contact with a menstruating woman.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she washed together with the Prophet from a single vessel while both were junub. The report continues in the next two entries without a chain of its own.

300.matn: and he would command me, so I would tie on the waist-wrapper (izār), and then he would have bodily contact with me while I was menstruating,
300.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the entry under the same chapter “Bodily contact with a menstruating woman.” The text has no chain of its own and continues ʿĀʾisha’s report from the previous entry: the Prophet commanded her to tie on the izār and then had bodily contact with her while she was menstruating.

301.matn: and he would put his head out to me while he was in iʿtikāf, and I would wash it while I was menstruating.”
301.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the entry under the same chapter “Bodily contact with a menstruating woman.” The text has no chain of its own and concludes ʿĀʾisha’s report: during iʿtikāf the Prophet put his head out to her, and she washed it while she was menstruating.

302.matn: Ismāʿīl ibn Khalīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn Mushir informed us, he said: Abū Isḥāq – that is ash-Shaibānī – informed us, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “When one of us was menstruating and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wished to have bodily contact with her, he would command her to tie on the waist-wrapper (izār) right at the onset of her menstruation, and then have contact with her. She said: And which of you controls his desire as the Prophet controlled his desire?” Khālid and Jarīr also transmitted it from ash-Shaibānī.
302.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Bodily contact with a menstruating woman.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet would command a menstruating woman to tie on the izār before he had bodily contact with her. She adds that none can control his desire as he did. At the end it is mentioned that Khālid and Jarīr likewise transmitted the report from ash-Shaibānī.

303.matn: Abū n-Nuʿmān narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, he said: Ash-Shaibānī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Shaddād narrated to us, he said: I heard Maymūna: “When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wished to have bodily contact with one of his wives, he would command her, and she would tie on the waist-wrapper (izār) while she was menstruating.” And Sufyān transmitted it from ash-Shaibānī.
303.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Bodily contact with a menstruating woman.” Maymūna reports that when the Prophet wished to have bodily contact with one of his wives, he would command her to tie on the izār, and that she did so while she was menstruating. At the end it is mentioned that Sufyān also transmitted the report from ash-Shaibānī.

304.matn: Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar informed us, he said: Zayd – that is Ibn Aslam – informed me, from ʿIyāḍ ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the prayer ground on the day of Aḍḥā or Fiṭr and passed by the women. He said: O assembly of women, give charity, for I was shown that you are the majority of the people of the Fire. They said: And why, O Messenger of Allah? He said: You curse often and are ungrateful to the spouse. I have not seen anyone deficient in intellect and religion who takes away the mind of a prudent man more than one of you. They said: And what is the deficiency of our religion and our intellect, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Is not the testimony of a woman equal to half the testimony of a man? They said: Yes. He said: That is from the deficiency of her intellect. Does she not abstain from prayer and fasting when she menstruates? They said: Yes. He said: That is from the deficiency of her religion.”
304.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The menstruating woman leaving the fast.” Abū Saʿīd reports that on one of the two ʿĪds the Prophet addressed the women and urged them to give charity, because he had been shown that they were the majority of the people of the Fire. He names frequent cursing and ingratitude to the spouse as the reasons. When they ask, he explains the “deficiency of intellect” by the testimony of a woman counting as half that of a man, and the “deficiency of religion” by her not praying or fasting while she menstruates.

305.matn: Abū Nuʿaim narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Salama narrated to us, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “We set out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioning nothing but Ḥajj. When we came to Sarif, I menstruated. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to me while I was weeping and said: What makes you weep? I said: By Allah, I wish I had not performed Ḥajj this year. He said: Perhaps you have menstruated? I said: Yes. He said: That is something Allah has decreed for the daughters of Ādam. So do what the pilgrim does, except do not circumambulate the House until you are pure.”
305.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The menstruating woman performs all the rites except circling the House.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she began to menstruate at Sarif and wept. The Prophet tells her this is something Allah decreed for the daughters of Ādam, and instructs her to do everything the pilgrim does except circumambulate the House until she is pure.

306.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, that she said: “Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubaysh said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: O Messenger of Allah, I do not become pure; should I abandon the prayer? The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: That is only a vein and not the menstrual period. When the period comes, leave the prayer; when its extent has passed, wash the blood from yourself and pray.”
306.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Prolonged bleeding (istiḥāḍa).” ʿĀʾisha reports that Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubaysh asked the Prophet whether she should abandon the prayer since she did not become pure. The Prophet answers that this is a vein and not the menstrual period; when the period comes she should leave the prayer, and afterwards wash off the blood and pray.

307.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Hishām, from Fāṭima bint al-Mundhir, from Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr, that she said: “A woman asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: O Messenger of Allah, what do you say: if the garment of one of us is touched by menstrual blood, how should she proceed? The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: If the garment of one of you is touched by menstrual blood, let her rub the spot, then sprinkle it with water, and then pray in it.”
307.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Washing off menstrual blood.” Asmāʾ reports that a woman asked the Prophet how she should proceed if her garment was touched by menstrual blood. He answers that she should rub the spot, sprinkle it with water, and then pray in it.

308.matn: Aṣbagh narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed me, he said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me that ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim told him: from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “One of us would menstruate, and then at her purification she would rub the blood off her garment, wash it, sprinkle the rest, and pray in it.”
308.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Washing off menstrual blood.” ʿĀʾisha reports that after menstruating, one of them would rub the blood off her garment, wash the spot, sprinkle the rest, and pray in it.

309.matn: Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: Khālid ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrima, from ʿĀʾisha: “One of his wives performed iʿtikāf with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while she had prolonged bleeding and saw blood. Sometimes she would put a basin beneath her because of the blood.” And he held that ʿĀʾisha saw safflower water and said: “It is as if this were something that so-and-so found in herself.”
309.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The hadith concerns the iʿtikāf of a woman with prolonged bleeding. ʿĀʾisha reports that one of the Prophet’s wives performed iʿtikāf with him although she saw blood and sometimes put a basin beneath her. At the end it is mentioned that ʿĀʾisha saw safflower water and remarked that it was like what the woman in question found in herself. The woman is not named in the text.

310.matn: Qutayba narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrima, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “One of the wives of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed iʿtikāf with him. She would see blood and yellowish discharge, with the basin beneath her, and she would pray.”
310.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: This hadith likewise concerns the iʿtikāf of a woman with prolonged bleeding. ʿĀʾisha reports that one of the Prophet’s wives performed iʿtikāf with him, saw blood and yellowish discharge, had a basin beneath her, and prayed.

311.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Muʿtamir narrated to us, from Khālid, from ʿIkrima, from ʿĀʾisha: “One of the Mothers of the Believers performed iʿtikāf while she had prolonged bleeding.”
311.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: This hadith likewise concerns the iʿtikāf of a woman with prolonged bleeding. ʿĀʾisha reports that one of the Mothers of the Believers performed iʿtikāf while she had prolonged bleeding. Her name is not given in the text.

312.matn: Abū Nuʿaim narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, he said: ʿĀʾisha said: “Each of us had only a single garment in which she menstruated. If any blood got on it, she would moisten the spot with her saliva and scrape it off with her fingernail.”
312.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “May a woman pray in a garment in which she menstruated?” ʿĀʾisha reports that they had only one garment in which they menstruated, and that they removed traces of blood with saliva and a fingernail.

313.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Ḥafṣa – Abū ʿAbdillāh said: or from Hishām ibn Ḥassān – from Ḥafṣa, from Umm ʿAṭiyya, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, she said: “We were forbidden to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband: four months and ten days. We did not apply kohl or perfume, and we did not wear a dyed garment except a ʿaṣb garment. And at the time of purity, when one of us had washed after her menstruation, we were permitted a little kusṭ-aẓfār. And we were forbidden to follow funeral processions.” He said: Hishām ibn Ḥassān transmitted it from Ḥafṣa, from Umm ʿAṭiyya, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
313.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Perfume for the woman when bathing after menstruation.” Umm ʿAṭiyya reports that women’s mourning for a dead person was limited to three days, but for a husband lasts four months and ten days, during which they used neither kohl nor perfume nor dyed garments other than a ʿaṣb garment. They were permitted a little kusṭ-aẓfār at purification after menstruation. They were also forbidden to follow funeral processions. Al-Bukhārī notes that he is unsure whether the narrator is Ayyūb or Hishām ibn Ḥassān, and at the end he cites Hishām’s transmission.

314.matn: Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from Manṣūr ibn Ṣafiyya, from his mother, from ʿĀʾisha: “A woman asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about her washing after menstruation, and he instructed her how to wash. He said: Take a piece (firṣa) with musk and cleanse yourself with it. She said: How shall I cleanse myself with it? He said: Cleanse yourself with it. She said: How? He said: Glory be to Allah, cleanse yourself! So I drew her to me and said: Follow the trace of the blood with it.”
314.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A woman rubbing herself when purifying from menstruation.” ʿĀʾisha reports that a woman asked the Prophet about washing after menstruation. He tells her to take a piece with musk and cleanse herself with it, and repeats it when she asks again. ʿĀʾisha draws the woman to her and explains that she should use it to follow the trace of the blood.

315.matn: Muslim narrated to us, he said: Wuhayb narrated to us, Manṣūr narrated to us, from his mother, from ʿĀʾisha: “A woman of the Anṣār said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: How do I wash after menstruation? He said: Take a piece (firṣa) perfumed with musk and cleanse yourself with it three times. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt shy and turned his face away – or he said: Cleanse yourself with it. So I took her, drew her to me, and told her what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, meant.”
315.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The bath after menstruation.” ʿĀʾisha reports that a woman of the Anṣār asked the Prophet how she should wash after menstruation. He tells her to take a piece perfumed with musk and cleanse herself with it three times, then feels shy and turns his face away. ʿĀʾisha takes the woman aside and explains what he meant.

316.matn: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ibrāhīm narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from ʿUrwa: that ʿĀʾisha said: “I entered iḥrām with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the Farewell Ḥajj, and I was among those who performed tamattuʿ and did not bring a sacrificial animal. And she said that she menstruated and did not become pure until the night of ʿArafa came. She said: O Messenger of Allah, this is the night of ʿArafa, and I had performed tamattuʿ with an ʿumra? The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Undo your hair, comb it, and hold off from your ʿumra. So I did. When I had completed the Ḥajj, he commanded ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān on the night of al-Ḥaṣba, and he had me perform an ʿumra from at-Tanʿīm in place of my ʿumra that I had begun.”
316.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A woman combing her hair when bathing after menstruation.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she performed tamattuʿ in the Farewell Ḥajj, menstruated, and did not become pure until the night of ʿArafa. The Prophet tells her to undo her hair, comb it, and hold off from her ʿumra. After the Ḥajj he had her brother ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān take her to at-Tanʿīm to perform an ʿumra in place of the earlier one.

317.matn: ʿUbayd ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Abū Usāma narrated to us, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “We set out at the sighting of the new moon of Dhū l-Ḥijja. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wishes to enter iḥrām for an ʿumra, let him do so; for had I not brought a sacrificial animal, I would have entered iḥrām for an ʿumra. Some entered iḥrām for an ʿumra and some for Ḥajj, and I was among those who entered for an ʿumra. The day of ʿArafa came upon me while I was menstruating, and I complained to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: Leave your ʿumra, undo your hair, comb it, and enter iḥrām for Ḥajj. So I did, until the night of al-Ḥaṣba came; then he sent my brother ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr with me, I went out to at-Tanʿīm and entered iḥrām for an ʿumra in place of my ʿumra.” Hishām said: In none of that was there a sacrificial animal, fasting, or charity.
317.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A woman undoing her hair for the bath after menstruation.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she was among those who entered iḥrām for an ʿumra and menstruated on the day of ʿArafa. The Prophet tells her to leave her ʿumra, undo her hair, comb it, and enter iḥrām for Ḥajj. Later she went with her brother to at-Tanʿīm and entered iḥrām there for an ʿumra in place of the earlier one. Hishām adds that none of this involved a sacrificial animal, fasting, or charity.

318.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿUbaydullāh ibn Abī Bakr, from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has appointed an angel over the womb, who says: O my Lord, a drop! O my Lord, a clinging clot! O my Lord, a lump of flesh! And when He wishes to complete its creation, he says: Male or female, wretched or fortunate, and what is the provision and the lifespan? And it is written in the belly of its mother.”
318.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “‘Formed and unformed.’” Anas reports from the Prophet that Allah has appointed an angel over the womb who announces the stages: a drop, a clinging clot, a lump of flesh. When Allah wishes to complete the creation, the angel asks about sex, about being wretched or fortunate, and about provision and lifespan, and this is written in the mother’s belly.

319.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: Al-Layth narrated to us, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “We set out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the Farewell Ḥajj. Some of us entered iḥrām for an ʿumra and some for Ḥajj. When we came to Mecca, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has entered iḥrām for an ʿumra and has not brought a sacrificial animal, let him leave iḥrām; whoever has entered for an ʿumra and has brought a sacrificial animal does not leave iḥrām until he leaves it with the slaughter of his animal; and whoever has entered for Ḥajj, let him complete his Ḥajj. She said: Then I menstruated and remained so until the day of ʿArafa, and I had entered only for an ʿumra. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded me to undo my hair, comb it, enter iḥrām for Ḥajj, and leave the ʿumra. I did that until I had completed my Ḥajj. Then he sent ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr with me and commanded me to perform an ʿumra from at-Tanʿīm in place of my ʿumra.”
319.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “How the menstruating woman enters iḥrām for ḥajj and ʿumra.” ʿĀʾisha reports on the Farewell Ḥajj: in Mecca the Prophet gave instructions for the ʿumra pilgrims with and without a sacrificial animal and for the Ḥajj pilgrims. She herself menstruated and remained so until the day of ʿArafa. The Prophet told her to undo her hair, comb it, enter iḥrām for Ḥajj, and leave the ʿumra; afterwards he had her perform an ʿumra from at-Tanʿīm with her brother ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān.

320.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: “Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubaysh had prolonged bleeding. She asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said: That is a vein and not the menstrual period. When the period comes, leave the prayer; when it passes, wash and pray.”
320.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The onset and end of menstruation.” ʿĀʾisha reports that Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubaysh had prolonged bleeding and asked the Prophet. He answers that this is a vein and not the menstrual period; when the period comes she should leave the prayer, and when it passes she should wash and pray.

321.matn: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Hammām narrated to us, he said: Qatāda narrated to us, he said: Muʿādha told me: “A woman said to ʿĀʾisha: Must one of us make up her prayer when she has become pure? She said: Are you a Ḥarūrī? We used to menstruate in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he did not command us to do it – or she said: and we did not do it.”
321.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The menstruating woman does not make up the prayer.” Muʿādha reports that a woman asked ʿĀʾisha whether a woman must make up her prayer once she is pure. ʿĀʾisha replies by asking whether she is a Ḥarūrī – meaning a follower of the Khawārij – and says that the women menstruated in the time of the Prophet and he did not command them to make it up. The narrator is unsure whether ʿĀʾisha said “he did not command us” or “we did not do it.”

322.matn: Saʿd ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to us, he said: Shaybān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, from Abū Salama, from Zaynab, the daughter of Abū Salama, who told him: Umm Salama said: “I menstruated while I was with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the blanket (khamīla). So I slipped out of it, took my menstruation clothes and put them on. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Have you menstruated? I said: Yes. Then he called me and brought me with him into the blanket.” She said: And she told me: the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would kiss her while fasting, and “the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I would wash from a single vessel after janāba.”
322.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Sleeping beside a menstruating woman in her clothes.” Umm Salama reports that she was lying with the Prophet in a blanket, menstruated, slipped away and put on her menstruation clothes, and that he called her and brought her with him into the blanket. She also reports that the Prophet would kiss her while fasting and that she washed with him from a single vessel after janāba.

323.matn: Muʿādh ibn Faḍāla narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, from Abū Salama, from Zaynab, the daughter of Abū Salama, from Umm Salama, she said: “While I was lying with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in a blanket (khamīla), I menstruated, so I slipped away and took my menstruation clothes. He said: Have you menstruated? I said: Yes. Then he called me, and I lay down with him in the blanket.”
323.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Sleeping beside a menstruating woman in her clothes.” Umm Salama reports that she was lying with the Prophet in a blanket, menstruated, slipped away and took her menstruation clothes, and that he called her, so she lay down with him again in the blanket.

324.matn: Muḥammad – that is Ibn Salām – narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb informed us, from Ayyūb, from Ḥafṣa, she said: “We used to forbid our young unmarried women (ʿawātiq) to go out on the two ʿĪds. A woman came and stayed at the residence of Banū Khalaf; she related from her sister – whose husband had taken part in twelve campaigns with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and my sister had been with him in six of them. She said: We used to treat the wounded and tend the sick. My sister asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: Is there any blame on one of us if she has no outer cloak (jilbāb) and therefore does not go out? He said: Let her companion lend her one of her cloaks, and let her take part in the good and in the call of the Muslims. When Umm ʿAṭiyya came, I asked her: Did you hear the Prophet say that? She said: May my father be ransom for him, yes! – and she never mentioned him without saying “may my father be ransom for him” – I heard him say: The young unmarried women and the secluded girls should go out – or: the young women who are secluded – and the menstruating women; let them take part in the good and in the call of the believers, and let the menstruating women keep away from the prayer place. Ḥafṣa said: I said: The menstruating women? She said: Do they not attend ʿArafa and this and that?”
324.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Menstruating women attend the two ʿĪds and the Muslims’ supplication and keep away from the prayer place.” Ḥafṣa reports that they used to prevent their young women from going out to the ʿĪds, and then relays the account of a woman whose sister asked the Prophet what to do if one has no outer cloak. He instructs that her companion should lend her one of hers. Umm ʿAṭiyya confirms, when Ḥafṣa asks, that the Prophet said that the menstruating women also go out, take part in the good and in the call of the believers, and keep away from the prayer place. To Ḥafṣa’s question about the menstruating women, Umm ʿAṭiyya replies that they do attend ʿArafa and other occasions.

325.matn: Aḥmad ibn Abī Rajāʾ narrated to us, he said: Abū Usāma narrated to us, he said: I heard Hishām ibn ʿUrwa say: My father told me, from ʿĀʾisha: “Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubaysh asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: I have prolonged bleeding and do not become pure; should I leave the prayer? He said: No, that is a vein. But leave the prayer for the number of days in which you used to menstruate, then wash and pray.”
325.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “If she menstruates three times in a month, and what women are believed in regarding menstruation.” ʿĀʾisha reports that Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubaysh asked the Prophet whether she should leave the prayer because of her prolonged bleeding. He answers that this is a vein, and tells her to leave the prayer for the number of days in which she used to menstruate, and then to wash and pray.

326.matn: Qutayba ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Muḥammad, from Umm ʿAṭiyya, she said: “We did not count the turbid and the yellowish discharge as anything.”
326.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Yellowish and turbid discharge outside the days of menstruation.” Umm ʿAṭiyya reports that they did not count turbid and yellowish discharge as anything significant.

327.matn: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, he said: Maʿn narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb told me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa and from ʿAmra, from ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Umm Ḥabība had prolonged bleeding for seven years. She asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he commanded her to wash, and said: That is a vein. So she would wash for every prayer.”
327.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The vein of prolonged bleeding.” ʿĀʾisha reports that Umm Ḥabība had prolonged bleeding for seven years and asked the Prophet about it. He commanded her to wash and said it was a vein. She then washed for every prayer.

328.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us: Mālik informed us, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, from his father, from ʿAmra bint ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: that she said to the Messenger of Allah: “O Messenger of Allah, Ṣafiyya bint Ḥuyayy has menstruated! The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Perhaps she will detain us. Did she not circumambulate with you? They said: Yes. He said: Then depart!”
328.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A woman who menstruates after the ifāḍa circuit.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she told the Prophet that Ṣafiyya bint Ḥuyayy had menstruated. He says that perhaps she will detain them, and asks whether she had not circumambulated with them. When they say yes, he says she should depart.
